Symptoms: pipe_rupture, over_pressure, thermal_decomposition

problems.problem_title: EUV sub-5nm node process integration consulting (CN client)
problems.problem_description: A major Shanghai-based foundry partner requires expert consulting on EUV-based sub-5nm process integration including gate-all-around (GAA) transistor formation, EUV double-patterning, and high-k metal gate (HKMG) deposition. Technology involves controlled EAR99-classification components. The client has secondary R&D presence in Portland, Oregon US. Multi-jurisdictional compliance review required.

problems.problem_title: 128-layer NAND 3D cell stacking yield improvement (CN fab + US IP)
problems.problem_description: A Wuhan-based memory fab is developing 128-layer 3D NAND cell stacking. Critical process steps involve tungsten-fill wordline etching and ALD-based high-aspect-ratio dielectric gap fill. U.S.-origin IP is incorporated in the cell array design. Expert must navigate both Korean NCT regulations and U.S. EAR part 734 restrictions. Multi-jurisdiction export compliance assessment required.

problems.problem_title: FinFET gate oxide reliability in multi-jurisdiction semiconductor project
problems.problem_description: A joint venture foundry operating across Shenzhen (CN) and Hsinchu (TW) requires expert consulting on HfO2 gate dielectric reliability for 7nm FinFET. Gate oxide TDDB failure rate exceeds specification. Controlled technology involves TCAD simulation tools under ITAR jurisdiction and HKMG deposition recipes with US-origin equipment. Expert must hold clearance compatible with both KR NCT and US EAR requirements.

problems.problem_title: DRAM capacitor ALD high-k stack for 1α node (cross-border IP)
problems.problem_description: A joint-venture memory R&D center co-located in Icheon KR and Chengdu CN requires specialist consulting for 1α-nm DRAM capacitor integration. ZrO2/Al2O3/ZrO2 (ZAZ) stack by ALD presents leakage current challenges. U.S. equipment EAR99 license concerns apply. Expert advice spans Korean NCT restrictions, US BIS license requirements, and China data security law. Dual-site jurisdiction conflict assessment mandatory.

problems.problem_title: Advanced packaging heterogeneous integration for AI chip export review
problems.problem_description: A fabless startup designing AI inference chips for Chinese hyperscale customers requires consulting on 2.5D SiP CoWoS-type advanced packaging. HBM3 memory integration with compute die raises ITAR concerns (US-origin IP in chiplet). Customer headquarters in Beijing, secondary design center in Austin TX. Consultant must be cleared for cross-border IP disclosure and NCT regulation.

problems.problem_title: HBM2E memory PHY signal integrity for CN cloud server ODM
problems.problem_description: A Ningbo-based ODM produces cloud server boards using HBM2E memory. Signal integrity failures occur at SerDes rates above 3.6 Gbps. The memory controller involves EAR99-listed US-origin SerDes IP cores. Consulting engagement covers Korean DRAM roadmap technology (NCT-controlled) and US BIS EAR Part 774 compliance for the memory subsystem. Multi-jurisdictional conflict expected between KR memory NCT and US EAR.

problems.problem_title: EUV photomask blank defect for Shenzhen litho facility — ITAR overlap
problems.problem_description: A Shenzhen-based EUV photomask blank manufacturer needs consulting on TaN/SiO2 absorber stack defect reduction. The mask inspection tool uses US-origin KLA e-beam technology potentially subject to EAR Part 744. Korean supplier provides SiO2 blank substrate involving NCT-adjacent IP. Expert must assess cross-border disclosure requirements for both KR and US regulations simultaneously — classic S4 jurisdictional conflict scenario.

problems.problem_title: Cu interconnect BEOL reliability for 3nm node (US-KR-CN tri-party)
problems.problem_description: A tri-party consortium (Samsung KR, GLOBALFOUNDRIES US, and SMIC CN) requires expert consulting on copper BEOL reliability at 3nm node: electromigration, stress voiding, and low-k dielectric cracking. US ITAR restrictions apply to GLOBALFOUNDRIES process IP. KR NCT regulations apply to Samsung's roadmap data. China data security law restricts outbound technical data flows. Three-way jurisdictional conflict requires SC loop re-evaluation across all expert candidates.

problems.problem_title: NCT-sensitive EUV scanner recipe optimization for advanced logic
problems.problem_description: Our advanced logic fab requires urgent recipe optimization for EUV scanner NA=0.33 with intra-field overlay improvement. Current overlay sigma >1.2nm exceeds 7nm node spec. Process involves Samsung-origin GAA integration IP and ASML EUV scanner with Korean NCT-classified recipe parameters. Multiple NCT-flagged expert candidates are expected in the shortlist. Need immediate review with full compliance pre-clearance.

problems.problem_title: 1β DRAM cell capacitance scaling with ZAZ high-k dielectric (NCT)
problems.problem_description: Our memory R&D team requires consulting on 1β-node DRAM capacitor integration using ZrO2-Al2O3-ZrO2 (ZAZ) high-k dielectric stack by thermal ALD. Target cell capacitance Cs > 20fF at <10nm equivalent oxide thickness. This is defined as national core technology per Korean Industrial Technology Protection Act Article 9. Only NCT-cleared experts eligible. High concentration of NCT experts expected.

problems.problem_title: GAA nanosheet uniformity across 300mm wafer (NCT-controlled IP)
problems.problem_description: Gate-all-around (GAA) nanosheet transistor channel uniformity is failing sigma > 0.8Å across 300mm wafer in our 3nm process. Si/SiGe superlattice channel etching and inner spacer ALD are the critical process steps. This process is registered as Korean National Core Technology set. Consulting engagement requires NCT pre-clearance for all specialist experts.

problems.problem_title: HBM3 through-silicon via (TSV) filling yield for AI HPC memory
problems.problem_description: Our HBM3 memory stack TSV (10μm × 100μm) copper filling yield rate is 94.2%, missing 99.5% specification. Void formation in via bottom during copper ECD and subsequent CMP overpolish are primary failure modes. Process is NCT-designated memory packaging technology per ITPA. Consultant pool has high NCT concentration in this specialty area.

problems.problem_title: EUV pellicle lifetime optimization for high-volume manufacturing
problems.problem_description: Our EUV pellicle (CNT-based, polysilicon substrate) is failing at accumulated dose of 18kJ/cm2 — well below the 100kJ/cm2 HVM target. Pellicle transmission drops from 90% to below 83% threshold. Pellicle technology is listed as EUV-related Korean NCT item under Semiconductor Special Act Article 12. Expected consultant pool is heavily concentrated in NCT-cleared EUV specialists.

problems.problem_title: V-NAND 238-layer cell array process NCT certification consulting
problems.problem_description: Our 238-layer V-NAND cell array integration requires expert certification consulting for NCT compliance. Channel hole etch aspect ratio exceeds 100:1. ONO (oxide-nitride-oxide) charge trap layer is key IP. V-NAND over 100 layers is designated Korean National Core Technology. All expert candidates must be NCT pre-cleared. Pool will be 70%+ NCT experts.

Our PIM-DRAM accelerator integrates analog multiply-accumulate (MAC) circuits within DRAM array periphery. This combination of in-memory computation with national-core-technology DRAM architecture creates dual NCT classification under Korean Semiconductor Protection Act. Only experts with both DRAM NCT clearance and AI accelerator expertise are eligible. NCT expert concentration expected >65% of candidate pool.

problems.problem_title: Intermittent device failure above 80°C with no pattern
problems.problem_description: Our packaged devices fail intermittently when ambient temperature exceeds 80°C. Failure mode shows no consistent pattern — random bit errors across different memory addresses. Failure rate jumps from 0.01% to 2.3% above this threshold. No morphological defects visible in SEM cross-section. Failure signature suggests atomic-level degradation mechanism. We need expert help to identify and fix the root cause.

problems.problem_title: Component swelling and discoloration after 500h at 95% humidity
problems.problem_description: Our electronic components show visible swelling and brown discoloration after 500 hours of 95% relative humidity exposure at 85°C. The swelling appears primarily at package corners and bond wire regions. Electrical continuity is maintained but resistance increases by 15-40%. Standard MIL-STD-883 humidity testing reveals systematic failure. Root cause identification and material remedy are required.

problems.problem_title: Write latency doubles after 10K program/erase cycles
problems.problem_description: Our storage product write latency degrades from 100μs baseline to over 200μs after approximately 10,000 program/erase cycles. Read latency remains stable. The degradation is non-linear — minimal change from 0-5K cycles, then rapid increase from 5K-10K. Refreshing the device with a vendor utility tool shows temporary recovery. No obvious controller firmware issue identified. Hardware root cause suspected.

problems.problem_title: Noise floor rises on read path above 1GHz operation
problems.problem_description: Our mixed-signal chip exhibits unacceptable noise floor rise on the read path when clock frequency exceeds 1GHz. At 800MHz baseline, SNR is 58dB. Above 1GHz the SNR drops below 45dB. Noise appears to be deterministic (not random) based on frequency spectrum analysis. Boards from two different foundries show the same behavior, suggesting a design-process interaction rather than manufacturing variation.

problems.problem_title: Catastrophic delamination events occurring stochastically in fab
problems.problem_description: Our production line experiences sudden catastrophic particle events occurring 2-3 times per week with no warning. After an event, the affected chamber shows extensive coating flaking on chamber walls. Particle counts jump from <5/wafer to >500/wafer instantaneously. The events seem to correlate with thermal cycling but not consistently. Chamber seasoning protocols have not resolved the issue.

problems.problem_title: Systematic center-to-edge pattern density dependency across 300mm
problems.problem_description: Our 300mm production line shows systematic center-to-edge variation in device electrical characteristics. Ring oscillator frequency varies by ±8% between wafer center and edge. This exceeds our ±2% spec. The variation correlates with die position but not with wafer orientation or lot-to-lot variation. Identical masks and equipment show the same pattern, suggesting a process physics root cause.

problems.problem_title: Soft failures at low supply voltage (0.6V) not reproducible at nominal
problems.problem_description: Our low-power IoT SoC exhibits soft failures exclusively at 0.6V supply (below 0.8V nominal). At nominal 0.8V, all tests pass. The failures are timing-related — data capture errors on critical path flip-flops — but SPICE simulation predicts 15% timing margin. Failures worsen at -20°C. Statistical analysis shows failures cluster in a specific silicon region suggesting systematic process variation.

problems.problem_title: Haze formation on substrate surface after wet cleaning step
problems.problem_description: After our standard SC1 wet cleaning step, silicon substrate surfaces develop visible haze when inspected under broadband illumination. The haze is not removed by subsequent cleaning steps. It appears only on substrates processed in batch mode, not in single-wafer processing. Haze density correlates with HF concentration and DI water resistivity but not with particle counts.

problems.problem_title: Sudden shift in electrical parametric test distribution in week 3
problems.problem_description: Our weekly parametric test data shows a sudden bimodal distribution shift starting from week 3 of Q2. Previously unimodal Vt distribution (sigma=28mV) split into two populations separated by ~80mV. Both populations pass individually but the split itself suggests a process excursion. The shift is time-correlated, not wafer-lot correlated, suggesting equipment or consumable root cause.

problems.problem_title: Early life failure rate spikes at 100-200h burn-in — no wear-out
problems.problem_description: Infant mortality failure rate on our power management ICs is unexpectedly high (0.8%) at 100-200 hour burn-in, dropping to near-zero at 500h. Classic bathtub curve infant mortality, but the peak is unusually large and delayed compared to industry norms. Failure analysis shows random single transistor opens in the power stage. No consistent photolithography or metallization defect. The failures appear post-crystallization suggesting a materials issue.
